questions.q: What is the value of x?
questions.why: Statement (1) gives x = 8. Statement (2) also gives x = 8. Each statement alone is sufficient.

questions.q: Is the integer n divisible by 6?
questions.why: Divisibility by 2 alone or 3 alone is insufficient. Together, an integer divisible by both 2 and 3 is divisible by 6.

questions.q: What is the value of y?
questions.why: Statement (1) gives y = 13. Statement (2) also gives y = 13. Each alone is sufficient.

questions.q: Is x positive?
questions.why: Statement (1) permits x = 4 or x = −4, so the sign is uncertain. Statement (2) establishes that x is negative, so the answer is definitely NO.

questions.q: What is the total number of employees in Departments A and B?
questions.why: Each statement gives only one department’s count. Together, the total is 28 + 37 = 65.

questions.q: What is the value of a?
questions.why: The ratio alone and the total alone are insufficient. Together, 8 ratio parts = 40, so one part is 5 and a = 3 × 5 = 15.

questions.q: Is the selling price greater than ₹1,000?
questions.s2: The profit is 30% of the cost price.
questions.why: Cost price alone does not determine selling price; profit percentage alone does not give the amount. Together, profit = ₹240 and selling price = ₹1,040, so YES.

questions.q: Is the average of four numbers greater than 12?
questions.s1: The sum of the four numbers is 52.
questions.why: Statement (1) gives an average of 52 ÷ 4 = 13, which is greater than 12. Statement (2) alone leaves the other three values unknown.

questions.q: What is the integer n?
questions.why: Statement (1) allows many even integers. Statement (2) gives n = 16 only, so Statement (2) alone is sufficient.

questions.q: Is a/b > 1?
questions.why: Statement (1) alone does not fix the ratio; Statement (2) alone does not constrain a. Together, a > b > 0, so a/b > 1.

questions.q: What is the value of x?
questions.why: Statement (1) leaves many possible pairs; Statement (2) gives y but not x. Together, x + 11 = 18, so x = 7.

questions.q: Did the business make a profit?
questions.why: Revenue alone and expenses alone are insufficient. Together, profit = ₹3,20,000 − ₹2,75,000 = ₹45,000, so YES.

questions.q: Is x = 6?
questions.why: Statement (1) allows x = 6 or −6. Statement (2) allows many positive values. Together, x² = 36 and x > 0 imply x = 6.

questions.q: Is the integer n divisible by 12?
questions.why: Divisibility by 3 alone or 4 alone is insufficient. Together, an integer divisible by both 3 and 4 is divisible by 12.

questions.q: Is x > 10?
questions.why: Statement (1) allows x = 8 (NO) and x = 11 (YES). Statement (2) guarantees x > 10, so it is sufficient.

questions.q: What is the value of x?
questions.why: Both statements express the same equation x + y = 12. Many values of x are possible, so even together they are insufficient.

questions.q: Is x positive?
questions.why: Statement (1) permits x = 5 or −5. Statement (2) gives x = 5, which is positive.

questions.q: Is the integer n odd?
questions.why: If n² is odd, n must be odd. An integer not divisible by 2 is also odd. Each statement alone is sufficient.

questions.q: Is the average of five numbers greater than 20?
questions.why: Statement (1) gives an average of 105 ÷ 5 = 21, so YES. Statement (2) alone does not guarantee an average greater than 20.

questions.q: Is x < y?
questions.why: Subtracting 3 in Statement (1) gives x < y. Dividing Statement (2) by positive 2 also gives x < y. Each alone is sufficient.

questions.q: What distance does a vehicle travel?
questions.s2: It travels for 2.5 hours at that constant speed.
questions.why: Statement (1) alone lacks time; Statement (2) alone lacks speed. Together, distance = speed × time = 60 × 2.5 = 150 km.

questions.q: How many days will Ravi take to complete a job alone?
questions.s1: Ravi and Sam together complete the job in 6 days.
questions.s2: Sam alone completes the job in 15 days.
questions.why: Together, their rate is 1/6 job per day; Sam’s rate is 1/15. Ravi’s rate is 1/6 − 1/15 = 1/10, so Ravi takes 10 days.

questions.q: What is the final price after a discount?
questions.s2: The discount is 15% of the marked price.
questions.why: Together, discount = 15% × ₹2,000 = ₹300. Final price = ₹2,000 − ₹300 = ₹1,700. Neither statement alone is sufficient.

questions.q: What is x?
questions.why: Neither statement alone determines x. Together, x + 5 = 14, so x = 9.

questions.q: How many students study both French and German?
questions.why: Statement (2) gives 40 students in the union. Together, overlap = 30 + 22 − 40 = 12.

questions.q: Is the conclusion “All managers are graduates” definitely true?
questions.s1: All department heads are graduates, and all managers are department heads.
questions.why: Statement (1) gives managers ⊆ department heads ⊆ graduates. Statement (2) directly says no manager is a non-graduate. Each alone establishes the conclusion.

questions.q: What is x?
questions.why: Together, 11 ratio parts equal 33, so one part is 3 and x = 4 × 3 = 12.

questions.q: What is the average of five numbers?
questions.s2: The average of the first four numbers is 16.
questions.why: Statement (1) gives the average as 85 ÷ 5 = 17. Statement (2) alone does not give the fifth number or the total.

questions.q: What is the smaller angle between the hour and minute hands at 3:00?
questions.s1: The minute hand points at 12 and the hour hand points at 3.
questions.s2: It is exactly 3:00 on a standard 12-hour clock.
questions.why: Statement (1) places the hands at 12 and 3, so the smaller angle is 90°. Statement (2) also fixes the time at 3:00, which gives a 90° angle. Each statement alone is sufficient.

questions.q: Is the year a leap year?
questions.why: Statement (1) alone is insufficient because century years must be divisible by 400. Statement (2) identifies 2000, which is divisible by 400, so it is a leap year.

choices.A: Statement (1) alone is sufficient, but Statement (2) alone is not.
choices.B: Statement (2) alone is sufficient, but Statement (1) alone is not.
choices.C: Both statements together are sufficient, but neither alone is sufficient.
choices.E: Even both statements together are insufficient.
